title: Granular reservation shares and latency-aware fallback PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers using Dedicated capacity ask for finer-grained guarantees than whole-node reservations. They want per-tenant shares inside a reserved pool, predictable degradation during bursts, and automated fallback that preserves latency SLOs for higher-priority tenants. This PRD defines a feature set to introduce granular reservation shares, latency-aware preemption/fallback behaviour, and admin controls for safe burst handling.
background: Current reserved pools are allocated as coarse slots or node counts per tenant. When pools saturate, traffic is throttled or evicted using blunt preemption heuristics that can produce uneven latency degradation and poor tenant experience. Sales and SREs report customers requesting: (1) proportional guarantees within a pool, (2) configurable failover to public/backup models, and (3) graceful throttling that biases preserving tail latency for pinned requests.
goals: 1) Allow tenants to reserve 'shares' within a reserved pool to express proportional throughput guarantees. 2) Implement a latency-aware fallback policy that routes excess requests to preconfigured fallback models/regions with preserved request metadata. 3) Provide admin controls and observability to tune share weights, preemption windows, and emergency reclaim policies.
scope_in_scope: API surface for defining share allocations inside existing Reserved Pools (percent or integer-credits)
Control plane UI/Console for visualizing pool composition and adjusting share weights
Runtime enforcement: scheduler changes to enforce shares and a latency-aware preemption routine
Fallback routing hooks to route overflow to alternate model variants/regions or public service endpoints
Metrics and dashboards: per-tenant effective throughput, tail latency (p50/p95/p99), preemption events
scope_out_of_scope: Billing rework for per-share metering (this will be accounted for in follow-up billing PRD)
Major GPU kernel/runtime changes unrelated to scheduling (quantization and kernel tuning are out)
Autonomous re-sharding of reserved nodes across zones (zonal balancing is separate project)
requirements: REQ-1: API to create/modify Reserved Pool with 'share' assignments: share can be specified as percentage (e.g., 60%) or integer credit count. Default behaviour preserves existing pool semantics if no shares set.
REQ-2: Scheduler must enforce minimum effective capacity per share in steady state and degrade proportionally when pool capacity is constrained.
REQ-3: Add a configurable preemption policy: allow 'soft-evict' windows where lower-share traffic is delayed or rerouted instead of hard-kill, with admin-settable preemption_priority tiers.

REQ-4: Latency-aware fallback: runtime should maintain per-request latency SLAs and, when a request is predicted to miss SLA due to queueing, optionally route to fallback target (model variant, different pool, or public API) preserving prompt, user_id, and routing metadata.
REQ-5: Console: expose per-pool breakdown, a 'what-if' simulator to preview allocation changes, and an incident timeline of preemption/fallback events.
REQ-6: Observability: emit events for share enforcement, queued-request counts, predicted SLA misses, fallback invocations, and successful completions; tags for tenant, pool, and priority.
REQ-7: Backwards compatibility: existing pools without shares must continue to operate unchanged; migrations optional and user-initiated.
REQ-8: Admin guardrails: safety knobs to cap total fallback volume (percentage of pool) and an emergency reclaim toggle for on-call.
REQ-9: API and console controls must be permissioned via existing RBAC; Private deployments must honor KMS/audit logging requirements for routing decisions.
tech_considerations: Scheduler: implement token-bucket style share enforcement or proportional queuing at the pool ingress to reduce head-of-line blocking.
Prediction: lightweight latency prediction model (e.g., percentile-based queuing estimate using current queue length + recent per-tenant execution time) to decide when to fallback.
Routing: fallback should use existing smart routing layer to select compatible model variants; include affinity and KV cache keys to avoid cold-cache regressions when possible.
State: maintain minimal per-tenant counters in control plane and runtime to avoid per-request DB hits; use in-memory sliding windows with periodic reconciliation.
Performance: enforce that share checks add <1ms median overhead to request admission in steady state.
Testing: simulate mixed workloads in staging with synthetic tenants to validate proportional degradation and fallback correctness.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Create/modify shares via API and Console for a reserved pool; changes take effect within the documented reconciliation window (<=60s).
AC-2: Under sustained load exceeding pool capacity, tenants receive throughput in proportion to configured shares within +-10% error margin over 5-minute windows.
AC-3: When queueing predicts SLA miss for a request from a lower-priority tenant, the system triggers fallback routing to the configured target and emits a fallback event with metadata.
AC-4: Admins can set a global fallback cap and emergency reclaim toggle; toggles operate immediately and are auditable via logs.
AC-5: Console shows per-tenant tail latency (p95/p99) and a timeline of preemption/fallback events with links to raw traces.
AC-6: Regression: median admission overhead for share enforcement is <1ms and p99 overhead <5ms compared to baseline.
success_metrics: SM-1: Reduction in hard-eviction incidents by 75% for customers using shares compared to similar pools without shares after 30 days.
SM-2: Customer-reported satisfaction score for Dedicated capacity handling >=4/5 in post-release NPS survey for participating customers.
SM-3: Fallback routing accuracy: >=95% of fallbacks preserve request context and complete successfully with acceptable cost impact (<=2x token cost on fallback).
SM-4: No SLO regressions for high-priority tenants in 90-day rollout window.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): internal-only pools + 3 pilot customers; verify share enforcement correctness and console UI flows (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (Beta): opt-in by customers via console + telemetry collection; limit fallback cap to 10% of pool for beta customers (4 weeks).
Phase 2 (General Availability): enable by default in Dedicated; provide migration tools and recommend share templates for common tenancy patterns (8 weeks).
Rollback: disable share enforcement and revert routing decisions if critical regressions found; emergency reclaim toggle available to SREs.
dependencies: ENG-31208: Scheduler ingress refactor to support pluggable admission policies
ENG-32411: Console metrics surface for per-tenant telemetry
ENG-32988: Smart routing fallback hooks and auth propagation
PM-100200: Billing alignment for share-based metering (follow-up)
